title: MZ I need help with my game's HUD!

posts.author: Sunny64
posts.body:
I'm not an expert on RPG Maker by any means, so I've stumbled upon this problem that I don't know how to solve... I'm using RPG Maker MZ, and after changing the resolution of my game, my HUD happens to be extremely large. Before making my battle system, I'd really love to fix this issue, so in the future it'll be more comfortable to work on the battle system.I'll attach 5 images of how the game looks rn, on the last two pictures, I've disabled all plugins. On the first 3, I'm using VisuStella's Core Engine, MainMenu Core, Message Core and Battle Core. There's one more image with the game's resolution.
I'd really appreciate any kind of help I can receive! Thank you all so much

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Why are you using such a small game window size? (not resolution)
There are a number of UI elements that have predefined sizes - the dimensions of faces, the size of the font, the padding on windows. If you decrease how much screen real estate you have and you don't re-code those things, then yes - your interface will take up proportionately more of your screen.
Those entries are really there for you to be able to size the window
up
, not down.

posts.author: Sunny64
posts.body:
Oh, I didn't know that...
I wanted to make my game in the same resolution that OMORI or Undertale have.
So I should code my own UI for this problem to be solved?
Thank you so much!

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Just as a technical note - again, we're not talking about resolution. We're talking about the size of the game window. Resolution is a measure of pixels per distance.
When you change the resolution of your monitor, it's still using the entire screen, but you're changing how many pixels it can display.
Here, you're just changing how much of the screen your window takes up, the pixels aren't any larger or smaller.
Sunny64 said:
I wanted to make my game in the same resolution that OMORI or Undertale have.

I would still ask why - what purpose does it serve? If you want to have pixelated art, you can do that perfectly well with a larger window. The only thing making your window small accomplishes is you make it harder for your players to see what's going on.
But to answer the question:
